summary: The Moirai runner image. It carries the runner daemon and the agent harness, not a project toolchain: a project that needs Go, Python, Docker or a build system asks for an execution image of its own.

tools.name: sh
tools.purpose: POSIX shell (BusyBox ash). `bash` is not installed, so shell scripts must be POSIX.

tools.name: git
tools.purpose: Version control. The workspace is a git worktree; the runner commits and pushes for you.

tools.name: ssh
tools.purpose: Reached by git for ssh:// and git@ remotes. You do not normally invoke it yourself.

tools.name: npm
tools.purpose: Node package manager. Installing globally fails: the image filesystem is read-only outside the workspace.

tools.name: npx
tools.purpose: Runs a package binary from the workspace's own node_modules.

tools.name: opencode
tools.purpose: The agent harness itself. Do not invoke it.

absent.name: python3
absent.note: No Python runtime. Use `node -e` where you would have reached for a one-line Python script.

absent.name: pip
absent.note: No Python packaging, because there is no Python.

absent.name: make
absent.note: No build system. Read the Makefile and run the underlying commands, or ask for an execution image that has it.

absent.name: go
absent.note: No Go toolchain. `go build` and `go test` cannot run here.

absent.name: docker
absent.note: No Docker client and no daemon socket. Nothing containerised can be built or run from inside a job.

absent.name: bash
absent.note: No bash. `#!/bin/sh` and POSIX syntax only.

absent.name: jq
absent.note: Not installed. Use `node -e` to read JSON.

absent.name: gcc
absent.note: No C toolchain, so no native build and no npm package that compiles on install.

absent.name: patch
absent.note: Not installed. Edit files directly, or use `git apply`.

notes: Standard BusyBox utilities beyond the ones listed -- sed, awk, grep, find, xargs, diff, gzip -- are available. Language runtimes and build tools beyond those listed are not.

This list is the environment's own declaration and is verified against the image when it is built, so it cannot drift from what is really installed. Trust it instead of probing: a command that fails because a tool is absent still costs a full attempt out of a budget of two.

The environment is fixed for the run. Do not try to install a missing tool -- everything outside the workspace is read-only in a normal deployment. Solve the task with what is listed, or report the work as blocked and name the tool you needed.
